analysis: Static reverse engineering; no sample was executed.

evidence.behavior: Creates hidden work directories, presents a topmost ransom lock screen, calls BlockInput, installs persistence, starts keylogging and background collection.

evidence.location: StartKeylogger RVA 0x33f0; HookCallback RVA 0x34a8; polling delegate RVA 0x3358
evidence.behavior: Installs a low-level keyboard hook and polls virtual keys 1 through 255, appending timestamps and keys to a log.
Reads key and clipboard logs into records, serializes them, and supplies form content to HttpClient.PostAsync.
Copies its executable to ready removable drives and writes executable AutoRun configuration; registers ms-settings DelegateExecute hijack and launches fodhelper.
Attempts read/encrypt/suffixed-write/delete in Desktop/TestFolder. The 17-byte AES key fails before encryption; the 15-byte IV would also be invalid. Existing attempt wording is appropriate.

samples.traits: Retained existing detections; their concrete behaviors and attempt limitations are supported.

evidence.behavior: Appends an Ed25519 administrator SSH key, sets its ACL, chooses an OS-compatible agent, downloads it with certutil, excludes it from Defender, and creates an auto-start service.

Encodes a TcpClient/IEX evaluator and schedules it hidden as SYSTEM every five minutes. Read bytes are discarded and IEX decodes a separate fresh zero array, so this is an attempted, broken socket-command channel.
Installs/starts OpenSSH, retrieves sshd configuration from the same remote controller, and permits inbound TCP/22.

samples.traits: Three specific hostile composites replace generic task-frequency conviction. Generic task and OS-query facts moved to neutral operation homes.

samples.identification: Elex resource dropper with digital-signing-tool facade

evidence.behavior: Runs hidden clone staging when no argument is present; otherwise calls resource extraction, and exits before the signing dialog if extraction succeeds.

The alphabet ekimhuqcroanflvzgdjtxypswb indexes rand()%26 for random filenames. Clones the executable to Temp, appends GetTickCount()&511 uninitialized heap bytes, launches a hidden ping-delayed shell, and exits.
Reads IMAGE resource 132, subtracts a+b/b/a cyclically using the original first two bytes, restores MZ, writes a random DLL, and starts rundll32 with QueryPluginInterface and the current module path.

evidence.location: Decoded DLL entry RVA 0x22000 -> SEH handler RVA 0x20e84 -> aPLib routine RVA 0x20db4
evidence.behavior: SEH patches the fault site into the unpacking path. Emulated only the isolated decoder and loader under Unicorn with stubbed APIs to recover bytes for static inspection.

evidence.location: Recovered QueryPluginInterface RVA 0xbb20; RVA 0x9050; RVA 0x72a0; RVA 0xb6a0
evidence.behavior: Exported entry starts background threads; recovered helpers register Run-key rundll32 activation, install service DLL configuration, retrieve remote content, and periodically decode remote configuration. Packed-stage reconstruction was sufficient for these static paths; no claim of successful live infection.

samples.traits: Two hostile findings: concealed decoded-resource launch and specific Elex clone/decoder fingerprint. Removed unsupported duplicate worm inference and corrected random-filename alphabet labeling.

controls.powershell: check.py: five positive/near-miss cases, including an inert comment example; maintenance tasks and ordinary SSH provisioning have no suspicious or hostile findings.
controls.native: Renaming retains both hostile findings. Erasing the resource-decoder routine removes both. Erasing only the plugin-command template removes the resource-launch objective while preserving the family fingerprint.
